messages:
alex.s: FYI customer reported intermittent 502s. our internal NLB target group shows most targets UNHEALTHY. customer is on Private VPC + k8s w/ Envoy ingress on 8443 (TLS).

jordan.cust: seeing 502s on our app when traffic spikes, but only for requests routed through Redwood private deployment. Health checks appear failing in the AWS console (Target->Unhealthy: connection timed out).

alex.s: Can you paste the ELB health check config? type/protocol/port/path etc.

jordan.cust: NLB (internal) -> health protocol: TCP, port 8443, interval 10s, healthy 2/unhealthy 2. Targets are node IPs (k8s nodes).

alex.s: ok. I suspect the NLB TCP probe isn't completing the TLS handshake and Envoy is dropping it. NLB TCP checks just open a TCP socket (no SNI). If Envoy expects SNI or enforces TLS client auth, that could fail.

marie.infra: also check security groups and node-level iptables. Internal NLB preserves client source IP, so SGs on nodes must allow the NLB subnets. If the node SG is too restrictive the probe won't get through.

sam.net: +1 on SGs. Also confirm service.externalTrafficPolicy is Local vs Cluster. With Local, health check hits node, with Cluster it can be DNATed to pod IP which can change behavior.

alex.s: jordan, can you run these from your bastion to reproduce?

  curl -v telnet://<nlb_ip>:8443
  openssl s_client -connect <nlb_ip>:8443 -servername gateway.internal

jordan.cust: ran them — telnet shows "Connected" then immediately "Connection reset by peer". openssl s_client fails with "no peer certificate" and handshake abort.

marie.infra: that matches TLS handshake abort. Do you have Envoy configured to require SNI or to reject connections without ALPN/SNI?

jordan.cust: Envoy listener has require_sni: true (we added for host scoping). Our ingress expects SNI to route to proper virtual host.

sam.net: There's the mismatch: NLB TCP health probe won't send SNI, so the probe will be dropped. Options: 1) change health check to HTTP on a plaintext path (ALB/HTTP) OR 2) add a plain-TCP acceptor on Envoy that responds OK without SNI, OR 3) configure k8s Service to use nodePort + target health endpoint that returns 200 over TCP.

alex.s: Quick workaround: add a simple TCP acceptor on port 8444 (no SNI, returns 200 on /health via HTTP) and point the health check at that port. Longer-term we should add a dedicated HTTP health path and set the service annotation so the LB uses HTTP health checks.

jordan.cust: we can change the AWS health check to port 8080 (non-TLS) but our service currently doesn't expose 8080 externally. We can patch the envoy config.

marie.infra: I pushed a small change to the helm chart to add a http_health port + /_hc endpoint bound to 127.0.0.1 (and a k8s readiness probe mapping). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR-254

alex.s: nice. Jordan, after you apply that patch, update the service annotation:

  service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: HTTP
  service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "8080"
  service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-path: "/_hc"

jordan.cust: applied PR and changed annotations. Health checks flipped to healthy within ~30s. No more 502s from customer.

sam.net: For docs: note that internal NLB TCP checks will not perform TLS handshake/SNI. If your ingress denies non-SNI connections, create a non-TLS health endpoint or use ALB HTTP(S) health checks.

alex.s: Also added a KB note to support runbook: "private-deployments: nlb-tcp-probe-tls-handshake" (ticket INFRA-678). Includes repro steps and remediation checklist (SGs, externalTrafficPolicy, health endpoint).

deploybot: deploy finished: infra/helm-chart@PR-254 -> prod (canary 100%) :white_check_mark:

jordan.cust: confirmed customer outage resolved. thanks all :tada:

alex.s: closing thread — keep an eye on metrics for a day and we'll follow up if it reappears.
